Scaled Dot-Product Attention is a particular attention mechanism proposed by Vaswani et al. in 2017. It is a type of attention function that computes the compatibility function using the dot product of the query with the corresponding key, and then applies a softmax function to obtain the weights on the values.

In the context of Scaled Dot-Product Attention, the input consists of queries and keys of dimension dk, and values of dimension dv. The attention function is computed as:

Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax([Q][K]^T / √dk) * V

where Q, K, and V are matrices of queries, keys, and values, respectively, and dk is the dimension of the keys and queries.

This attention mechanism is used in the Transformer model, which relies entirely on self-attention to compute representations of its input and output without using sequence-aligned RNNs or convolution.

Positional encoding in the Transformer is a mechanism used to inject information about the relative or absolute position of tokens in a sequence into the model. This is necessary because the Transformer model contains no recurrence and no convolution, and therefore cannot make use of the order of the sequence on its own.

The positional encoding is added to the input embeddings at the bottoms of the encoder and decoder stacks. It has the same dimension as the embeddings, so that the two can be summed. The Transformer uses sine and cosine functions of different frequencies to create the positional encoding:

_PE_ ( _pos,_ 2 _i_ ) = _sin_ ( _pos/_ 10000 [2] _[i/d]_ [model] )

_PE_ ( _pos,_ 2 _i_ +1) = _cos_ ( _pos/_ 10000 [2] _[i/d]_ [model] )

where _pos_ is the position and _i_ is the dimension.

This function is chosen because it allows the model to easily learn to attend by relative positions, since for any fixed offset _k_, _PEpos_ + _k_ can be represented as a linear function of _PEpos_ [Vaswani et al. 2017, pp.6].

generated_answer:
A pooling layer is a type of layer in Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) that aims to gradually reduce the dimensionality of the representation, thereby reducing the number of parameters and the computational complexity of the model [O'Shea and Nash 2015, pp.8].

The pooling layer operates over each activation map in the input and scales its dimensionality using the "MAX" function, typically in the form of max-pooling layers with kernels of a dimensionality of 2 × 2 applied with a stride of 2 along the spatial dimensions of the input [O'Shea and Nash 2015, pp.8]. This scales the activation map down to 25% of the original size while maintaining the depth volume to its standard size.

The role of the pooling layer is to perform downsampling along the spatial dimensionality of the given input, further reducing the number of parameters within that activation [O'Shea and Nash 2015, pp.5]. This helps to reduce the complexity of the model and improve its performance.

Sentences are encoded using byte-pair encoding (BPE) [3], which has a shared source-target vocabulary of about 37,000 tokens (Source: [Vaswani et al. 2017, pp.7]).
